newsitem.title: USA: Armstrong seeks meeting with Domco.
newsitem.headline: Armstrong seeks meeting with Domco.

text.p: Armstrong World Industries Inc said Wednesday it had sent a letter to Domco Inc seeking a meeting to review Armstrong's C$23-per-share takeover offer.
Armstrong Chairman George Lorch sent the letter to John Claxton, chairman of the Special Committee of Independent Directors of Domco.
In the letter, Lorch said the Armstrong offer provides Domco investors with fair value and equal treatment.
He said a proposal by Sommer Allibert SA has no immediate or long-term value for Domco's minority shareholders and does not have the same potential for Domco's Canadian businesses.
Sommer, Domco's controlling shareholder, plans to merge its floor covering business, which includes Domco, with Tarkett AG.

Lorch said Sommer will have serious difficulty resolving the unavoidable conflict between its Domco and Tarkett subsidiaries because the subsidiaries have separate minority shareholder interests that compete.

He suggested that the special Domco committee recommend that all shareholders, including Sommer, accept Armstrong's offer, and that committee members resign from the Domco board if Sommer does not ensure that it will offer the minority Domco shareholders C$23 per share.
Domco, a Canadian company, created the special committee to consider Armstrong's offer, first announced on June 9. The panel is expected to make its recommendation in early July.
Lorch's letter urged the special committee not to be cowed by the influence of Sommer, a French car parts maker that owns 69 percent of Domco.
Armstrong makes floor and wall coverings.
